eps_desc: The default is the latest per-share earnings the snapshot has. A fiscal-year figure is marked beside the label.
rdcf_growth_desc: The EPS growth rate you expect. Green means it sits below the actual ten-year annualised EPS growth; red means above.
dcf_growth_in_the_next_desc: The growth stage defaults to 10 years at the reported 10-year growth, negative included. When that history cannot be used, the rate stays empty for you to fill in. Its value is that stage discounted to today.
rdcf_freecashflow_growth_tips_title_neg: Your expected growth rate may be achievable
book_desc: Default Book Value is the tangible book value, which may underestimate or overestimate the real value
rdcf_growth_tips_neg: Expected 10-Year EPS without NRI Growth rate < Actual Historical 10-Year EPS without NRI Growth Rate
rate_live_note: The risk-free rate is the local 10-year government yield for the cash-flow currency, rounded up, plus 6 percentage points. Hong Kong dollar cash flows use the US 10-year as a proxy.
rate_bundled_note: The discount rate uses a saved 10-year government bond yield. You can adjust it.
rate_cached_note: Discount rate uses a cached 10-year yield.
discount_rate_desc: The default is the local 10-year government yield for this cash-flow currency, rounded up, plus 6 points. Hong Kong dollar cash flows use the US 10-year as a proxy because the local benchmark series has ended. The display currency does not change the discount rate. If no local yield is available, the default falls back to 8% and says so. You can also set your own required return, commonly 6%–20%.
discount_currency_note: The default discount rate uses the local 10-year yield for this cash-flow currency, not the display currency.
search_for_your_stocks: Please enter a company name/ stock ticker.
rdcf_freecashflow_growth_tips_neg: Expected ten-year annualised FCF per share growth <= actual ten-year annualised FCF per share growth
price_edit_here: Edit the price in the header; changes apply only to this page.
compare_lead: Up to five, highest margin of safety first, one shared set of defaults
compare_step_add: Type a symbol above, then press Enter or Add.
compare_step_second: A second name is what makes the margin of safety comparable.
compare_one: One more symbol and the wider margin of safety is marked.
compare_note: One cross-section under the default assumptions; open a stock page to change them. Ranked first is not a buy call.
compare_dup: Those symbols are already in the comparison
total_freecashflow_desc: Defaults to the latest free cash flow per share the sources can supply. Earnings and free cash flow stay separate; neither overwrites the other.
business_predictability_desc: The share of years with positive earnings. Not an outside rating, and not a gate on whether this valuation can be used.
rdcf_freecashflow_growth_tips_title_pos: Your expected growth rate may be unreachable
rdcf_growth_tips_title_neg: Your expected growth rate may be achievable
name: Name
fair_value_desc: Future earnings under the chosen model, discounted to a per-share value today. The large figure is the middle; the line under it is the same assumptions tightened and loosened. A rough reference, not a price target.
rdcf_freecashflow_growth_tips_pos: Expected ten-year annualised FCF per share growth > actual ten-year annualised FCF per share growth
rdcf_implied_desc: The annualised first-stage growth that would make the intrinsic value equal the current price, under the same assumptions. It is not the adopted growth used to compute the intrinsic value, and it is not the historical rate.
rdcf_growth_tips_title_pos: Your expected growth rate may be unreachable
dcf_terminal_desc: The second stage defaults to 10 years at 4%; the year after is capitalized at that rate (at most two points under the discount rate) and discounted in. When that growth is not below the discount rate, only the two finite stages count.
rdcf_growth_tips_pos: Expected 10-Year EPS without NRI Growth rate > Actual Historical 10-Year EPS without NRI Growth Rate
symbol_format_hint: Format: EXCHANGE:CODE, e.g. SHSE:601398 or NYSE:KO
no_records_yet: No records yet. Use "Record this valuation" to save one.
record_measure_note: Returns and risk follow the record series; with shares they use the position method (flows included), otherwise prices only.
margin_of_safety_desc: How far the price sits below the intrinsic value, as a share of it. Negative means the price is above it.
sensitivity_hint: Discount rate and growth each move two points around the current assumption; the centre cell is the current case.
sensitivity_note: tint = margin of safety against the price
wacc_desc: Cost of equity = risk-free + beta × equity premium + size premium, rounded to a whole percent. There is no debt and no tax here, so this is not WACC.
model_help: Ordinary companies discount per-share earnings, or free cash flow that belongs to shareholders. Banks, insurers and brokers use residual income: the return on book fades to the discount rate.
pin_source: Pin a source for this symbol
multiple_check_hint: Apply a target multiple to the per-share base to see the price the market would pay.
long_run_pe: If earnings stay here, 12× is {price}. A no-growth cross-check, not the intrinsic value.
banner_error: Every data source failed · no quote this time
banner_fallback: Primary source is down, this came from {providers}
growth_adopted_note: Historical growth {historical}%{window}. The first stage fades from {adopted}% down to the second-stage rate, rather than holding {adopted}% flat.
growth_capped_note: Historical growth {historical}%{window}. The default does not extrapolate that pace and underwrites at most {cap}%. The first stage fades from {adopted}% down to the second-stage rate.
growth_window: ({from}–{to}. Earlier years are left out of the growth rate after a unit break)
growth_missing_note: No growth history. Nothing is filled in.
growth_refused_note: After a split or a unit break, too few years remain. Nothing is filled in.
stage_horizon_note: Both stages cover {years} years. The years after that are capitalized at the second-stage rate.
stage_rate_note: Second-stage growth is not below the discount rate, so later cash flows do not shrink in present value. The years after the two stages are not capitalized; the horizon stays finite.
tbv_double_count_note: Tangible book and earnings are two views of the same assets. Adding book into the intrinsic value counts those assets twice.
reverse_unavailable: Implied growth has no solution when the per-share base is not positive.
basis_unavailable: This basis has no per-share figure in the snapshot, so it is not used.
reverse_no_solution: No growth rate in range makes the intrinsic value match this price.
fcf_basis_fcff: This is firm free cash flow, and net debt is not subtracted. It is not an equity value, so this basis stays off.
fcf_basis_ocf: Banks and insurers have no free-cash-flow figure. Operating cash flow is not used.
residual_income_note: Financial institutions use residual income: today's return on book fades to the discount rate, so the extra return does not last forever. One end of the range is that return continuing.
fcf_basis_invest: This is not shareholder free cash flow. The figure approximates operating cash flow minus investing cash outflow (OCF − investing outflow), so it includes acquisitions and financial investments, not just capital spending. The components are not broken out on this site; check the filing for them. Do not treat this as the default valuation base.
fcf_basis_equity: Free cash flow is operating cash flow minus capital spending, divided by shares.
fcf_basis_none: The statements on file carry no capital spending, so free cash flow is not shown. Value this one on earnings.
chart_empty: This snapshot has no series to plot.
own_note: from the loaded quote and per-share bases
own_hint: For reference only; none of these change the intrinsic value.
click_row_hint: click a row to switch the chart below
converted_note: Results are converted to {currency} (≈); inputs stay in native {native}
about_lead: Open a stock to see its published valuation and margin of safety. Then try your own assumptions.
about_sources_body: Eastmoney supplies most quotes and financials for mainland China and Hong Kong. US financials mainly come from SEC EDGAR. Published valuations use the financial data and government bond yields recorded for each release.
about_license_body: ValueProbe’s code is open source under the MIT licence. Each data source sets its own terms.
about_sources_timing: The release date, financial period and quote date are shown separately. The margin of safety uses the displayed quote. Enter your own price to see how the margin changes.
about_feedback_body: If a quote, financial figure or valuation looks wrong, include the ticker, the date shown on the page and a source we can check.
home_lead: Enter a symbol to see what the business is roughly worth, and how much growth the price already assumes.
continue_where: Pick up where you left off
continue_empty: nothing here yet — open a stock and it will show up.
continue_empty_step: Use Try above, or type a symbol in the header.
sum_lead: The price and the per-share bases.
sum_open_dcf: Value it on the DCF model →
name_as_reported: Company names are shown as the data source reports them, untranslated
watchlist_hint: stored on this device, for coming back to what you follow
watchlist_empty: No watchlist yet — open a stock and tap the star at the top right.
watchlist_step_find: Type a symbol in the header and open its valuation.
watchlist_step_star: Use the star beside the name. That is what adds a row here.
watchlist_one: Add a second name to compare margins of safety.
watch_nothing: No importable symbols in that file
rows_failed: The prices did not load this time.
footer_tagline: valueprobe · a local-first, open-source intrinsic value calculator
footer_note: Research use only, not investment advice.
peer_compare_hint: Current P/E and P/BV of listed peers, and the price their median implies.
peer_compare_note: cross-check only, click a name to open it
peer_implied: The median peer P/E implies {price}, {gap} versus the DCF intrinsic value; the bases differ.
peer_unavailable: Peer quotes are unavailable right now
discount_hkd_proxy_note: The Hong Kong 10-year benchmark is empty, so the default discount rate uses the US 10-year Treasury as a proxy.
discount_fallback_note: No local 10-year yield is available for this cash flow, so the default discount rate has fallen back to 8%. Adjust it to your required return.
